title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the list of 'éléments de structure' attached to a typical situation (X, D, J). The likely setting: an algebraic curve X over a number field with a cusp divisor D. I is the set of cusps (points of D). J is a set of distinguished (rational) points. X' is an étale cover. G' is a finite group acting on X'. 𝒢' is an extension 1→G'→𝒢'→Γ, with Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q) or an open subgroup. Over an open subgroup Γ'⊂Γ there is a germ of lifting Γ'→𝒢'. A universal cover X̃'→X' is chosen, with π1(X') = Aut(X̃'/X'). This gives an extension 1→π1(X')→ℰ'→𝒢'→1. ℰ' acts on the sets X̃'(I) and X̃'(J) of points of the universal cover over cusps and over the points of J, equivariantly over I and J.

(6) An ℰ'-equivariant map Φ: X̃'(I) → Hom(T(Q̄), π1(X')), where T(Q̄) = lim μ_n = Ẑ(1). Each point of the universal cover lying over a cusp gives its inertia subgroup, which is canonically a quotient of Ẑ(1) via the local monodromy. ℰ' acts on the target in two ways: on T(Q̄) through ℰ'→𝒢'→Γ (cyclotomic character), and on π1(X') by inner automorphisms of ℰ' (normality of π1 in the extension (3)). The margin warns that this is the description only when dim X = 1. Otherwise the 'situation must be revisited in more detail', since at normal-crossing strata the inertia is Ẑ(1)^r and more structure is needed.

(7) A system of maps Ψ_j: X̃'(J) → Splitt(ℰ'_j/𝒢'_j), j∈J. Here 𝒢'_j is the stabilizer (decomposition group) of j and ℰ'_j is its preimage in ℰ'. A point of the universal cover over j gives a splitting of ℰ'_j→𝒢'_j: the arithmetic section attached to a rational or decomposition point, as in the section conjecture. Equivariance is given by the formula (g·u)(σ) = g · u(ḡ⁻¹σḡ) · g⁻¹, with ḡ the image of g in 𝒢'. This transports a section over 𝒢'_j to a section over 𝒢'_{gj} = ḡ𝒢'_jḡ⁻¹.

(9) Records the germ of homomorphisms ℰ'→𝒢'→Γ together with a lifting Γ'→ℰ' over an open subgroup. This is a germ of section defined only up to shrinking Γ, presumably coming from a base point or a model over a finite extension.

The purpose, per the next page, is a complete 'gruppentheoretisches Gleichnis': describe all these structures purely group-theoretically and recover X from Γ-data. This is the anabelian programme in an early, systematic form.
errors: No mathematical error found. The equivariance formula is correct for g carrying j to gj: for σ ∈ 𝒢'_{gj}, ḡ⁻¹σḡ lies in 𝒢'_j, and conjugating by g gives a lift of σ.

Minor imprecision: the text says 'compatible avec opérations de ℰ'_j'. Restricted to ℰ'_j the formula gives an action on Splitt(ℰ'_j/𝒢'_j) itself. The global ℰ'-compatibility of the whole system Ψ requires letting g move j, which the formula in fact handles.
For Φ, 'Hom' should really be read as continuous homomorphisms in the profinite setting. In higher dimension the single-generator inertia description fails, as Grothendieck himself notes.

ideas.what: Equivariant assignment to each point over a cusp of its inertia homomorphism Ẑ(1)→π1, with Galois acting on Ẑ(1) via the cyclotomic character and on π1 by conjugation.
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal inertia subgroups / branch cycle structure; cyclotomic equivariance of inertia (used in Belyi-type and Ihara-type rigidity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (SGA1 tame ramification theory); Fried's branch-cycle argument (1977); Nakamura's and Tamagawa's group-theoretic characterization of cuspidal inertia (1990s)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (tame fundamental group, Exp. XIII); implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Points of J (rational or decomposition points) give splittings of the arithmetic fundamental group extension over their decomposition groups, equivariantly.
ideas.modern_name: Section map X(K) → {sections of π1(X)→G_K}/conjugacy (section conjecture setup)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 27 June 1983 (published in Geometric Galois Actions 1, 1997); Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Working with a finite automorphism group G' and a semilinear extension 1→G'→𝒢'→Γ that admits only a germ of splitting over an open subgroup, then pulling back to ℰ'.
ideas.modern_name: Field of moduli vs field of definition via extensions of Galois groups; Galois action on Hurwitz-type data
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated much later)

ideas.what: Remark that in dimension >1 the inertia structure at the boundary must be re-examined.
ideas.modern_name: Higher-dimensional anabelian geometry / normal crossings inertia Ẑ(1)^r (e.g. for moduli spaces M_{g,n})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Mochizuki (anabelian results for higher-dimensional varieties)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses M_{g,n} and the Teichmüller tower but not in this form

missed.claim: An early (c.1980-81, pre-Faltings letter) systematic list of anabelian 'structure elements'. It already includes the section map for points as an equivariant system of splittings and the cyclotomically twisted inertia map at cusps, together with a germ of section over an open subgroup of Γ. Historically it documents that the section-map formalism was in place before 1983.
missed.quote: Ψ = (Ψ_j)_{j∈J} : X̃'(J) → Splitt(ℰ'_j/𝒢'_j) ... (gu)(σ) = g u(ḡ⁻¹σḡ) g⁻¹
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical dating of the section conjecture formalism; the mathematics itself is now standard.

missed.claim: The extension 1→G'→𝒢'→Γ with only a germ of lifting Γ'→𝒢' anticipates the later field-of-moduli formalism. In that formalism, obstructions to descending a G-cover are read off from splittings of such Galois extensions (Dèbes–Douai).
missed.quote: Γ' ⊂ Γ ss-groupe ouvert, avec flèche Γ' → ℰ'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Suggests Grothendieck integrated field-of-moduli and descent questions into the anabelian 'Gleichnis' from the start. The later literature developed this separately. This is speculative given the uncertain meaning of G'.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard anabelian setup (arithmetic fundamental group extension, cuspidal inertia with cyclotomic twist, sections from points), carefully written down. Its interest is chiefly historical (early date, systematic 'structure elements', germ-of-section formalism), not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'opérant des les deux de droite par : op.' should read roughly 'opérant sur les deux de droite par : op. sur T(Q̄) via (𝒢' via Γ) et sur π1(X') [via automorphismes intérieurs dans (3)]'.
In (7) the domain is X̃'(J) (capital J, the set), not X̃'(j).
The heading of (7) is 'Syst. d'applications' (inserted 'Syst. d'' above 'application').
'g_{g'}' is Grothendieck's notation for the image of g in 𝒢' (i.e. ḡ = g_{𝒢'}), not a separate element.
'Splitt(ℰ'_j(𝒢'_j))' in the 'où' clause should be Splitt(ℰ'_j/𝒢'_j).
Margin (top left) reads 'si dim X = 1 ; sinon il faut revoir encore plus en détail la situation....'.
Crossed-out marginal note bottom left: roughly 'si 𝒢' agit ... stabilisateurs dans 𝒢', ℰ' ... à remplacer dans (8) ... dans "pfeilwand"(?) (7) ... compatibles avec ... des ℰ'' — largely illegible.
